text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

* South African Breweries and its Namibian partners have almost zero chance of being given the thumbs up by government to open a N$100 million brewery at Oshakati with Trade and Industry minister Hidipo Hamutenya saying that as far as he is concerned government's position on the matter remains unchanged.
* Namibia's national soccer team has gone on strike over the Namibian Football Association's failure to honour payment promises to players, jeopardising this weekend's away match against Tunisia.

* Since independence, government debt has risen by eleven percent. According to the Commercial Bank of Namibia this does not include the N$1.6 billion inherited debt, which has by now been written off by the South African government.

* Former fighters of the South West Africa Territory Force (SWATF) and the insurgency unit Koevoet are still complaining that government does not treat them as citizens of Namibia and they therefore are without jobs and homes and have to live in poverty.

* Nurses employed at Windhoek's two state hospitals are demanding N$19 million from the government in outstanding overtime payment and have threatened a strike if the money is not paid out by the end of this month.
